fish.name: Kettle Guppy
fish.flavor: Thrives at temperatures that would poach a lesser fish. Locals swear the ones from the hottest pools arrive pre-cooked, which has never once been true.

fish.name: Soot Darter
fish.flavor: Leaves little grey smudges on your hands, your tackle box, and somehow your face. Washes off in the springs it came from, which feels like a racket.

fish.name: Cinder Chub
fish.flavor: Round, cheerful, and pleasantly warm to the touch. The unofficial mascot of every bathhouse on the caldera road.

fish.name: Steamskipper
fish.flavor: Skips across the surface film where the mist is thickest. Nobody has ever actually seen one land, and asking about it makes the old anglers go quiet.

fish.name: Basalt Bream
fish.flavor: Grey as the rock it hides against, and about as talkative. Catching one feels like winning an argument with the landscape.

fish.name: Sulphur Smelt
fish.flavor: Smells exactly how you'd expect. Grilled over coals with a squeeze of lemon, it smells marginally better and tastes like a fond memory.

fish.name: Pebblemouth
fish.flavor: Carries warm pebbles around in its mouth. Naturalists insist it's nesting behaviour; locals insist it just likes them.

fish.name: Poachfin
fish.flavor: Named by a cook, not a naturalist. Does a lazy backstroke through water that visibly simmers, entirely at peace with its situation.

fish.name: Ash Minnow
fish.flavor: Schools drift through the shallows like ash on a slow wind. One is nothing; a hundred is weather.

fish.name: Boilerbelly
fish.flavor: Its belly glows faintly pink after a good hot soak, which is always. Serene, spherical, and just slightly smug about it.

fish.name: Rustgill
fish.flavor: Its gills are stained orange by the iron-rich springwater. Old-timers say a rusty gill means an honest fish, though nobody remembers who checked.

fish.name: Springside Loach
fish.flavor: Dozes in the warm shallows like a cat in a sunbeam. Looks genuinely betrayed when hooked, then forgives you almost immediately.

fish.name: Copper Vent Eel
fish.flavor: Coils around underwater vents to keep its blood warm, gleaming like fresh pipework. Tarnishes if you lie to it, allegedly.

fish.name: Geyser Perch
fish.flavor: Times its leaps to the geyser eruptions and rides the column for a full breathtaking second. An incorrigible show-off, beloved by everyone.

fish.name: Mudpot Catfish
fish.flavor: Wallows contentedly in the burping grey mudpots. Its whiskers can taste the difference between mud and very slightly different mud, a gift it refuses to explain.

fish.name: Obsidian Flounder
fish.flavor: Flat, black, and glossy as knapped glass. Handle it with the respect you'd give a dropped knife.

fish.name: Fumarole Goby
fish.flavor: Nests inside warm rock chimneys and peers out at passersby like a tiny disapproving landlord. The dots along its flanks glow when the vent below exhales.

fish.name: Scalding Carp
fish.flavor: The bathhouse keeper feeds them rice from the veranda, and has for forty years. They are enormous, ancient, and entirely unbothered by your lure.

fish.name: Tuff Puffer
fish.flavor: Inflates when startled, which in constantly bubbling water is always. Lives its entire life mildly alarmed and somehow thriving.

fish.name: Flinthead Sculpin
fish.flavor: Its skull is plated like struck flint, and it headbutts anything that enters its crevice on principle. Respected, if not exactly liked.

fish.name: Glassblower's Grayling
fish.flavor: Its dorsal fin swirls like molten glass caught mid-turn. The old craftsmen up the hill claim its ancestors escaped from a furnace, and refuse to elaborate.

fish.name: Old Kettlejack
fish.flavor: Every village pool claims their own Kettlejack. This one has three hooks in his lip, a torn fin from the flood year, and your grandfather's initials scratched on one of the hooks.

fish.name: Pyroclast Pike
fish.flavor: Strikes from the murk with the speed of a lava bomb and roughly the same manners. Locals fish for it in pairs, mostly for the moral support.

fish.name: Weeping Basalt Ray
fish.flavor: Trails warm mineral tears from its wingtips as it glides across the pool floor. Bathers say a brush against your ankle means good fortune and a mild burn, in that order.

fish.name: Magmavein Char
fish.flavor: Orange lines run beneath its skin like slow lava through cooling stone. It stays warm in your hands long after the catch, like a stone from the hearth.

fish.name: The Caldera Widow
fish.flavor: She has outlived four eruptions, two bathhouses, and every angler who ever bragged about hooking her. The black ribbon of her dorsal fin is the last thing the bragging ones mention.

fish.name: Grandmother Cinder
fish.flavor: The oldest catfish in the springs, grey as banked coals and twice as patient. Villagers leave rice cakes at the water's edge on cold mornings, and the cakes are always gone by noon.

fish.name: Slagheart
fish.flavor: A fish of cooled slag with something molten still beating inside. Blacksmiths consider it very good luck and very bad eating.

fish.name: Old Scald
fish.flavor: They say the great pool never freezes because Old Scald sleeps at the bottom of it. They say a lot of things, but the claw-deep gouges on the bathhouse pier support most of them.

fish.name: The First Warmth
fish.flavor: Before the volcano, before the isles, something warm curled up at the bottom of the world, and the water learned kindness from it. It is still down there, still curled, still teaching.
